title: Anatomical plasticity across species reflects willingness to confabulate in morphospace

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Anatomical plasticity across species reflects willingness to confabulate in morphospace

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Levin proposes that the spectrum from hardwired, mosaic C. elegans through intermediately plastic amphibians and embryonic mammals to extremely plastic planaria reflects a strategic parameter: the willingness to confabulate in anatomical space, i.e. to rely on pattern extraction and completion rather than taking genetic priors too seriously.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 4. Beyond the Brain: Bowties Everywhere

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: What underlying parameter is represented by the spectrum ranging from the hardwired, mosaic C. elegans to the intermediately plastic amphibia and (embryonic) mammals, and to the extreme plasticity of planaria? I propose it is the willingness to confabulate in anatomical space

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2024), doi:10.3390/e26060481; section “4. Beyond the Brain: Bowties Everywhere”. Scope: Metazoans from C. elegans to amphibians, mammals and planaria

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-memory-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.42

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Comparative plasticity can be measured, but equating it with confabulation and pattern completion is interpretive. Public evidence covers many examples yet is heterogeneous and cannot cleanly establish the proposed strategic parameter.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Construct a preregistered cross-species plasticity index from recovery after standardized anatomical perturbations and test whether it covaries with pattern-completion performance after controlling for phylogeny and experimental effort. A monotonic nematode-to-planarian gradient supports the proposal.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Species differ in assay availability and injury type.

Willingness to confabulate is a metaphor requiring a new index.

Phylogeny and publication effort strongly confound rankings.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.35
data adequacy: 0.4
discriminating power: 0.3
operationalizability: 0.4
data existence: 0.6

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The plasticity ordering itself is a familiar comparative description. The proposed underlying parameter, willingness to confabulate and to discount genetic priors, does not name an observation that would come out differently from ordinary differences in mosaic versus regulative development. The claim is a reinterpretation, not a separable empirical statement.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Regulative versus mosaic development can be ranked from embryological experiments, but no result would show that the ranking is a willingness to confabulate rather than a difference in developmental constraint.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The spectrum from C. elegans to planaria mixes developmental mode, genome, and regenerative ecology.

Confabulation in anatomical space has no measure distinct from regulative capacity.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.15
data adequacy: 0.25
data existence: 0.3
operationalizability: 0.25
analysis feasibility: 0.3
